access_control.scope: Matches the normalized mount-relative path /health and /health/*, so it covers every mounted application's health route, including the auth application's external /auth/health.
access_control.policy: The client address must be loopback or private (RFC 1918, IPv4 and IPv6 loopback, fc00::/7, fe80::/10). HEALTH_TRUSTED_CIDR adds comma-separated ranges; invalid entries are logged and skipped.
access_control.denial: 403 with {"error": "Health endpoints restricted to private networks"} and a warning log carrying the address, path and method.
access_control.sessions: The shipped site.session.skip_paths list keeps /health, /health/advanced, /auth/health, /api/v1/status, /api/v2/status and /api/v3/status from minting a session. An operator-defined list replaces the shipped one.

evidence.note: scope, trusted ranges, the environment variable and the denial response
the middleware is installed for every mounted application
the shipped session skip_paths list
the same list as the boot fallback

records.status_codes: 200; 403 when the address is not trusted
records.payload: status (always the literal "ok"), timestamp (epoch seconds), version
records.probes: none. The status value is a constant, so a 200 here means the process served a request, not that its dependencies are reachable.

records.access: Route declares auth=noauth; the health middleware restricts it to loopback and private addresses.
records.status_codes: 200 for both ok and degraded, because the handler sets no status; 403 when the address is not trusted
records.payload: status (ok or degraded), timestamp, version, checks.keydb, checks.jobqueue, checks.authdb, checks.secret_verifier. Each check carries its own status and, where applicable, a password-masked url, a vhost, a mode, a state or an error message.
records.probes: keydb with a datastore PING; jobqueue by opening a broker connection with 5-second connect and read timeouts, reported as not_configured when jobs are disabled, no URL is set or the client library is absent; authdb with a connection test, reported as not_configured unless the auth database is loaded and connected; secret_verifier from the boot-cached verifier state, re-probed read-only when boot could not reach the datastore. Checks reporting not_configured are excluded from the overall status, which is ok only when every remaining check is ok and degraded otherwise.

evidence.note: the four checks, the overall-status rule and URL masking
route and auth attribute

records.access: Served only while the auth application is mounted, which is Full mode. The health middleware restricts it to loopback and private addresses, because it arrives mount-relative as /health. In other modes nothing routes the path and it returns 404.
records.status_codes: 200; 503 when the handler raises; 403 when the address is not trusted; 404 when the auth application is not mounted
records.payload: On success: status (the literal "ok"), timestamp, database (ok, error or not_required), version, mode. On failure: status ("error"), error, timestamp.
records.probes: The Rodauth database connection, when one is configured. status stays "ok" even when database reports error, so read the database field rather than the top-level status.

evidence.note: the response body, the database field and the 503 branch
the /auth mount prefix
why the mount-relative match covers this path, and the 404 in other modes
